title: land's scope stop records its ops row under step rebase, not scope
goal: a land run that stops at step scope records its land.step row with step=scope, so backlog.py ops and the retrospective name the real stop

run: import sys,re; t=open("_tools/bl_land.py",encoding="utf-8").read(); ok=re.search(r"ops_mark\(\"scope\"\)",t) is not None; print("scope step marked:",ok); sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

repro_reason: the stop needs a code-lane landing with a branch whose commit changes a file outside its touches against a remote; SP-jplczvj2's ST-oo6uxbn6 landing printed 'land stopped at step scope' while backlog.py ops showed step=rebase exit=1
